notes: The 90th, 99th and 99.9th percentiles are user-requested hypotheses, not observed tiers. We have not measured a representative population of AI users.

nodes.question: How do ordinary businesses use AI to handle many small tasks?
nodes.why_ask: The San Francisco Fed documents a wide range: email, grant writing, market research, operations and pricing, as well as some owners who develop client-facing AI software.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Owners can spot neglected but costly operational tasks because they encounter the failures personally. Writing a grant or adjusting a price is less impressive than an autonomous research agent, but its value depends on whether the result survives actual business review.

nodes.question: Why might an expert reject apparently more autonomous coding?
nodes.why_ask: Ronacher reports that long autonomous coding loops can increase complexity and weaken understanding despite producing substantial output.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: A long autonomous loop can increase completed output while decreasing the maintainer's understanding of invariants, coupling, and design intent. The hidden cost emerges when modifications must be explained or repaired after the generation session.
nodes.transferable_insight: Compare maintainability after a week, not just generated line count or initial completion time. This is a first-person engineering critique, not a controlled estimate of typical losses.

nodes.question: What have our own ChatGPT-plus-GitHub projects actually taught us?
nodes.why_ask: Real viewer and question-tree workflows include source-linked research, repository edits, usability revisions, a GitHub API 404 and a mistaken-repository edit subsequently reverted.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: The navigation project provides a direct example of whole-system inefficiency: repeated interface redesign, wrong-target edits, and debugging overhead can consume benefits from fast code generation. GitHub commits and reports make the sequence inspectable, but no counterfactual time saving has been measured.
nodes.transferable_insight: An agent's effectiveness includes choosing the correct repository, preserving working behavior, capturing user-visible failure signals, and recovering accurately. A passing isolated edit cannot substitute for a usable end-to-end interaction.

nodes.question: Why did 16 parallel agents manage to build a large C compiler?
nodes.why_ask: Report documents nearly 2,000 Claude Code sessions and roughly $20,000 in API costs producing ~100,000 lines of Rust compiler code capable of compiling Linux 6.9 across architectures.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Separate Docker/Git workspaces and task locks reduced collisions over individual files, but did not create independent problems by themselves. When agents converged on one Linux kernel failure, GCC-assisted compilation of controlled file subsets exposed smaller failures that workers could address separately. The evaluator helped restructure the task rather than merely score an answer.
nodes.transferable_insight: Parallelism pays when failure isolation produces independently solvable and independently checkable tasks. Compiler correctness comes from real compilation and execution evidence, while reported build success still leaves bootstrapping, optimization, code quality, and resource efficiency unresolved.

observed_trace.what: Set an ambitious compiler functional target and significant structural requirements.
Run agents in persistent loops, isolated Docker workspaces, Git clones and task-file locks; work is pulled and merged.
observed_trace.evidence: S-CARLINI 'Enabling long-running Claudes'; 'Running Claude in parallel'

observed_trace.what: Design compiler tests, quality gates, concise structured errors, random/quick test subsamples and accumulated progress records.
observed_trace.evidence: S-CARLINI 'Write extremely high-quality tests'; 'Put yourself in Claude's shoes'

observed_trace.what: All agents hit the same monolithic Linux kernel compilation failure; changes collided rather than adding useful parallel work.
Use GCC to compile controlled subsets of kernel files, narrowing failing combinations and allowing different agents to work on different offending files.
Compiler reportedly built Linux and other projects, but used GCC for 16-bit x86 bootstrapping and assembler/linker; output efficiency and Rust quality remained weaker than mature alternatives.

nodes.failure_to_intervention: Sixteen workers encountered the same monolithic kernel-compilation obstruction; GCC-based file-subset isolation transformed it into several distinguishable failures.

nodes.question: How did a researcher outside the specialty build a cosmology solver with AI?
nodes.why_ask: JAX cosmological Boltzmann solver project used CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, Git, a CLASS reference implementation, and repeated numerical comparisons; not production-grade across all regimes.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: A dependency-coupled cosmological solver requires error localization across numerical stages; independent agents can multiply inconsistent partial fixes. The author preserved a plan and failures in CLAUDE.md/CHANGELOG.md, then compared numerical output against CLASS to guide predominantly sequential diagnosis.
nodes.transferable_insight: External numerical oracles can make an unfamiliar scientific task approachable, but agreement on some outputs does not imply scientific validity across the parameter space. The oracle's coverage and a human's ability to reason about coupled errors remain constraints.

observed_trace.what: Set requirements: fully differentiable JAX cosmological solver and initially 0.1% desired accuracy relative to CLASS.
Use a CLAUDE.md plan and a CHANGELOG.md log of progress, failed attempts, accuracy and limits.
observed_trace.who: human and agent jointly maintained representation

observed_trace.what: Compare numerical outputs against CLASS, commit recoverable units and keep a persistent compute process.
observed_trace.who: human-designed validation loop executed by model
observed_trace.evidence: S-CLAX 'The test oracle'; 'Git as coordination'; 'Execution loop'

observed_trace.what: Use predominantly sequential, causal diagnosis; coupled solver stages make unstructured independent parallel tasks less effective.
Reach sub-percent agreement on some outputs; gaps in parameter coverage and science-domain conventions limit full reliability.

nodes.failure_to_intervention: Coupled numerical stages favored sequential diagnosis against CLASS over unstructured independent parallel changes.

nodes.question: How does AlphaEvolve turn LLM ideas into validated algorithm improvements?
nodes.why_ask: A mix of LLM-generated programs, automated evaluators, stored candidates and evolutionary selection; DeepMind reports algorithm improvements deployed in its infrastructure.

nodes.question: Why did experts sometimes become slower when AI was available?
nodes.why_ask: Across 246 real issues in developers' familiar codebases, allowing early-2025 AI tools increased observed completion time by 19%; developer expectations were for speedup.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: In the published early-2025 task setting, developers experienced overhead from using and reviewing AI help despite expecting speedups. The observed 19% slower completion is an end-to-end result; the precise contribution of individual causes has not been isolated.
nodes.transferable_insight: Measure time from problem understanding through accepted, correct integration—not model output speed. Familiarity with a codebase may make reviewing plausible generated changes more expensive than solving the issue directly.

nodes.question: Should agents do everything, or know when to involve humans?
nodes.why_ask: Propose 'Twilight Factory' in which agents proactively seek human approval, expertise and judgment rather than maximizing unattended autonomy.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: The 'Twilight Factory' proposal changes the agent's goal from operating without humans to deciding when human approval, expertise, or judgment is required. This is an organizational design hypothesis, not evidence of measured superiority.
nodes.transferable_insight: Escalation should be treated as a control policy that can be evaluated on consequential decisions, missed interventions, and review cost; more autonomous action is not necessarily more useful.

causal_hypotheses.question: Are better outcomes explained mainly by domain expertise?
causal_hypotheses.plausible_mechanism: Experts can identify the right problem, cheaply reject nonsense and supply missing assumptions.
causal_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: Novices using an economical workflow achieve comparable novel outcomes on the same task family.

causal_hypotheses.question: Does an executable evaluator explain more than prompt quality?
causal_hypotheses.plausible_mechanism: A test oracle turns uncertain output into an iterative search process.
causal_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: Adding realistic tests/evaluators does not improve final quality after equalizing attempts, human time and compute.

causal_hypotheses.question: Does autonomy buy capability or mostly scale and hidden work?
causal_hypotheses.plausible_mechanism: Agents progress while humans are absent, but risk building wrong things or expensive review debt.
causal_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: Comparable finished tasks show stable efficiency and quality gains independent of pre-existing infrastructure.

causal_hypotheses.question: Is ordinary high-leverage use often task selection rather than sophisticated orchestration?
causal_hypotheses.plausible_mechanism: Knowledge of local work identifies consequential low-cost opportunities.
causal_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: Operational benefits vanish after including repairs and human acceptance.

causal_hypotheses.question: Do AI collaborations leave transferable human competence?
causal_hypotheses.plausible_mechanism: Debugging, explanation, experiments and revisitable artifacts create learning.
causal_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: No-AI transfer tasks and one-month maintenance require just as much assistance as before.

mechanism_comparison.question: What actually determines whether more independent agents help on a difficult engineering problem?
mechanism_comparison.status: observed contrast, not controlled causal conclusion

rsm_trajectory.detail: A task is a dependency graph; parallelism helps where tasks and evaluations can be decoupled, while strongly coupled errors require causal tracing.
Hypothesis A: number of agents is decisive; B: task factorization and evaluator make agents productive; C: domain knowledge is the chief limitation; D: resources dominate.
Would one excellent agent with a robust oracle outperform many poorly coordinated agents on a coupled task?

Carlini directly reports 16 agents converging on the same kernel problem and introducing GCC-assisted file-level bisection; Mishra-Sharma explicitly favors sequential causal diagnosis for his tightly coupled solver. This supports, but does not prove, the dependence-structure explanation.

carlini_observed_trace.what: Set an ambitious compiler functional target and significant structural requirements.
Run agents in persistent loops, isolated Docker workspaces, Git clones and task-file locks; work is pulled and merged.
carlini_observed_trace.evidence: S-CARLINI 'Enabling long-running Claudes'; 'Running Claude in parallel'

carlini_observed_trace.what: Design compiler tests, quality gates, concise structured errors, random/quick test subsamples and accumulated progress records.
carlini_observed_trace.evidence: S-CARLINI 'Write extremely high-quality tests'; 'Put yourself in Claude's shoes'

carlini_observed_trace.what: All agents hit the same monolithic Linux kernel compilation failure; changes collided rather than adding useful parallel work.
Use GCC to compile controlled subsets of kernel files, narrowing failing combinations and allowing different agents to work on different offending files.
Compiler reportedly built Linux and other projects, but used GCC for 16-bit x86 bootstrapping and assembler/linker; output efficiency and Rust quality remained weaker than mature alternatives.

mishra_sharma_observed_trace.what: Set requirements: fully differentiable JAX cosmological solver and initially 0.1% desired accuracy relative to CLASS.
Use a CLAUDE.md plan and a CHANGELOG.md log of progress, failed attempts, accuracy and limits.
mishra_sharma_observed_trace.who: human and agent jointly maintained representation

mishra_sharma_observed_trace.what: Compare numerical outputs against CLASS, commit recoverable units and keep a persistent compute process.
mishra_sharma_observed_trace.who: human-designed validation loop executed by model
mishra_sharma_observed_trace.evidence: S-CLAX 'The test oracle'; 'Git as coordination'; 'Execution loop'

mishra_sharma_observed_trace.what: Use predominantly sequential, causal diagnosis; coupled solver stages make unstructured independent parallel tasks less effective.
Reach sub-percent agreement on some outputs; gaps in parameter coverage and science-domain conventions limit full reliability.

competing_explanations: An oracle is the enabling capability, whether parallel or sequential.
Task coupling explains the effective organizational structure.
Agent quality, cost and initial domain experience drive more of the difference than organization.
The two projects are too different to support a causal explanation without further tests.
mechanism_comparison.cheapest_discriminating_probe: Take an existing real systems-code issue containing multiple independent failures and a different issue with one tightly coupled end-to-end failure. Hold model and quality requirements constant; compare one agent with multiple agents using the same time/compute budget, then repeat with an oracle that partitions failures. Record successful fixes, regression rate, engineer intervention and integration time.
mechanism_comparison.certificate_status: source-bounded contrast; not a confirmed cross-domain rule

case_presentation.purpose: Surface observed mechanisms and consequential decisions, not just topic labels.
case_presentation.evidence_rule: Observed traces are source-bounded. Missing decisions and unobserved failures remain explicitly unknown. Comparison records are hypotheses, not established causal estimates.
case_presentation.comparison_rule: Render mechanism_comparison once as linked research shared by the participating cases; do not duplicate the long comparison in each case.
